html:
The Emirate of Transjordan was set up in 1921 under Abdullah, a son of the Sharif of Mecca who had led the Arab Revolt. It was the start of the state of Jordan.

Britain held the land east of the Jordan river under its mandate for Palestine. When Abdullah arrived with followers, apparently to fight the French in Syria, Winston Churchill offered him the land as an emirate, kept apart from the promise of a Jewish homeland west of the river. Abdullah made Amman, then a small town, his capital. A British-led army, the Arab Legion, kept order.

Transjordan became independent as a kingdom in 1946 and took the name Jordan in 1949. Abdullah was murdered in Jerusalem in 1951. His grandson Hussein became king.
